tc01.steps:
Load SonicOS firmware and boot with default settings.
Go to the VPN > Advanced page and click the 'Configure' button under IKEv2 Settings.
tc01.title: Default IKE attributes in a Global IKEv2 Policy
tc01.description: This test verifies that the Global IKEv2 Policy is created by default with the following attributes for IKE proposal. DH Group=2, Encryption=3DES, and Authentication=SHA1.
tc01.result:
The Configure IKEv2 Dynamic Client Proposal dialog is displayed.
It shows the following attributes for IKE proposal: DH Group=2, Encryption=3DES, and Authentication=SHA1.

tc02.steps:
Load SonicOS firmware and boot with default settings.
On the VPN > Settings page, add a new VPN policy. Select IKEv2 exchange mode and enter 0.0.0.0 IPSec gateway.
View the Proposals tab of the VPN policy.
tc02.title: IKE attributes in IKEv2 dynamic peer policy.
tc02.description: This test verifies that attributes for IKE proposal in a VPN policy with IKEv2 exchange mode and zero IPSec gateway are greyed out.
tc02.result: The attributes for IKE proposal in the VPN policy are greyed out.

tc03.steps:
Load SonicOS firmware and boot with default settings.
On the VPN > Settings page, add a new VPN policy. Select IKEv2 exchange mode and enter 0.0.0.0 IPSec gateway. Make sure that attributes for IKE proposal are greyed out and show DH Group=2, Encryption=3DES, and Authentication=SHA1.
On the VPN > Advanced page, click the Configure button under IKEv2 Settings.
In the Configure IKEv2 Dynamic Client Proposal dialog, change Encryption to AES-128 and click OK. Click OK in the popup message "Global IKEv2 proposal modofication updates IKEv2 dynamic peer policies and deletes current tunnel for those policies. Are you sure you want to update global policy?"
Open the VPN policy created in Step2 and view the Proposal tab.
tc03.title: Modify IKE attributes in the Global IKEv2 Policy.
tc03.description: This test verifies that IKE attributes in a VPN policy with IKEv2 exchange mode and zero IPSec gateway should be modified in the Global IKEv2 Policy.
tc03.result: The Encryption has been changed to AES-128 in the IKEv2 dynamic peer policy.

tc09.steps:
Load SonicOS 4.0 ENH firmware on SonicWALL1 and SonicWALL2, and boot with default settings. Configure LAN and WAN interfaces on the firewalls.
On the VPN > Settings page of SonicWALL1, add a new VPN policy. Select IKEv2 exchange mode, enter 0.0.0.0 IPSec gateway, and select X0 subnet of SonicWALL1 as a local network and X0 subnet of SonicWALL2 as a destination network.
On the VPN > Settings page of SonicWALL2, add a matching VPN policy. Select IKEv2 exchange mode, enter X1 IP address of SonicWALL1 in the primary IPSec Gateway address field. Select X0 subnet of SonicWALL2 as a local network and X0 subnet of SonicWALL1 as a destination network.
Initiate ping from PC2 to PC1.
tc09.initial: PC1 --- X0 SonicWALL1 X1 --- X1 SonicWALL2 X0 --- PC2
tc09.title: Negotiate a tunnel using a VPN policy with IKEv2 exchange mode and zero IPSec gateway.
tc09.description: This test verifies that IKE and IPSec tunnel can be created using a VPN policy with IKEv2 exchange mode and zero IPSec gateway.
tc09.result: IKE and IPSec SAs are negotiated. The tunnel between local and remote LANs is created.

tc32.steps:
Import certificates on two FWs. The two FWs support AESGCM in phase 1 .
Add ikev2 s2s vpn policy on two FWs. Auth method is 3rd party certificate. DUT's gw is 0.0.0.0. Fill correct peer ike id. Set local and remote network. Proposal phase 1 uses DH group 14 + AESGCM16-256 + PRF_HMAC_SHA256 which configured in dynamic client proposal. Peer's gw is DUT's x1, not 0.0.0.0.
After tunnel up, ping from PC under local network to remote network.
tc32.result: Tunnel can up. PCs can ping each other.

tc34.steps:
Factory default FW, FW's version is after story GEN7-35748.
Add ikev2 dynamic client tunnel vpn policy from CLI, set gateway as 0.0.0.0 and peer ike id.

config(2CB8ED9D80F0)# vpn policy tunnel-interface 111

tc14.steps:
Load SonicOS firmware on SonicWALL1 and SonicWALL2, and boot with default settings. Configure LAN and WAN interfaces on the firewalls.

On the VPN > Settings page of SonicWALL1, add a new VPN policy. Select IKEv2 exchange mode, enter 0.0.0.0 IPSec gateway, Configure the Peer IKE ID” edit box in IKE Authentication part, set the value as X1 IP address of SonicWALL2.
And select X0 subnet of SonicWALL1 as a local network and X0 subnet of SonicWALL2 as a destination network. Set IKE SA lifetime = 270 sec, IPSec SA lifetime = 120 sec.

On the VPN > Settings page of SonicWALL2, add a matching VPN policy. Select IKEv2 exchange mode, enter X1 IP address of SonicWALL1 in the primary IPSec Gateway address field. Select X0 subnet of SonicWALL2 as a local network and X0 subnet of SonicWALL1 as a destination network. Set matching SA lifitime.

4. Initiate ping from PC2 to PC
Let four minutes pass and view the log on the firewalls.
tc14.initial: PC1 --- X0 SonicWALL1 X1 --- X1 SonicWALL2 X0 --- PC2
tc14.title: Rekey event for the tunnel using VPN policy with IKEv2 exchange mode and zero IPSec gateway.
tc14.description: This test verifies that IKEv2 dynamic peer policy is renegotiated  when IKE/IPSec lifetime expires.
tc14.result: Child SAs are negotiated after SA lifetime is about to expire. IPSec SA is renegotiated in 120 seconds. IKE SA is renegotiated in 270 seconds.
